Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to provide users with a way to move their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Here are the details.

iOS will make app replacement easier

Although it's uncommon, developers sometimes retire an existing app and replace it with a new one, requiring users to move to a separate, standalone app.

While most developers try to make the transition seamless, the migration process may still require some action from the user, especially when it comes to data that isn't stored in the cloud.

With iOS 27.2, Apple will address this issue with a system-managed migration flow that can move an app's data and supported settings to a designated replacement app before deleting the old one.

Based on code currently available in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following prompt:

The developer recommends moving the data and settings from your existing "%1$@" app to the new "%2$@" app. iPhone can now do this for you before you get started with the new app. When finished, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone.

Users can then choose to "Move App Data & Settings" or "Move Nothing." If a user declines to migrate, iOS will show a second confirmation warning that notes some preferences — including notification and location settings — may need to be reconfigured.

It's worth noting that this feature appears to be limited to developers replacing their own apps with a designated replacement app, rather than migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a range of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, Location, and Health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • App-specific Do Not Disturb and Focus Mode settings
  • App Lock and Protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and accessory Live Activities
  • Access to relevant accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, camera-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll keep an eye out for updates to this framework throughout the iOS 27.2 beta testing period, and will report back as we discover more about how developers are implementing this functionality.
